# Logistics and supply chain

## Scope

Applies when the change touches shipments, warehouses, trading-partner EDI, or product traceability. Not when the product moves no goods and exchanges no trade documents; a shop's checkout and stock are commerce. Neighbours: `aidd-team:commerce-and-marketplaces`, `aidd-team:apis-and-services`, `aidd-team:data-and-analytics`.

## Terms

- **GTIN and SSCC**: The number of a trade item, and the serial number of one logistics unit, such as a pallet or a parcel.
- **Incoterms rule**: Which party pays and bears the risk on each leg of a shipment, such as FCA or DDP.
- **Interchange**: One batch of EDI documents, such as orders, ship notices, or invoices, with its control number.
- **Due diligence statement**: The EUDR statement the first operator files before a covered product enters or leaves the EU market; later operators and traders keep its reference.
- **Product passport**: A product's data, such as its materials and origin, reached through an identifier on it.

## Invariants and missed cases

| Always true | The case a plan misses |
| --- | --- |
| A shipment moves only along its allowed states, once per event. | A delivered scan before the shipped scan, or a carrier resending an event. |
| An EDI interchange is processed once, however often it arrives. | A partner resending an interchange with the same control number after a lost acknowledgement. |
| Every quantity carries its unit of measure, and every conversion is explicit. | Cases read as each units, or kilograms as pounds. |
| A covered product reaches the EU market only with its due diligence reference. | A lot split or blended after the statement was filed. |
| A dangerous-goods item ships only on a mode whose rules allow it, with its UN number and class (IATA DGR, ADR, IMDG). | A lithium battery booked as general cargo on an air leg. |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | Name the goods, the markets, and the trading partners. A covered commodity's product on the EU market is in EUDR scope; an EV, light-transport, or industrial battery needs a passport. | S1, S2 |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | Every consignee, shipper, and end user is screened against the sanctions and denied-party lists on the route, and a controlled item names its classification before it ships. | S8 |
| Specify | One shipment state machine with its carrier events; each logistics unit has an SSCC and each item a GTIN; the Incoterms rule names who holds the risk on each leg. | S7, S4, S6 |
| Specify | A due diligence reference travels with each EUDR lot through every split and blend, and each lot's origin is traced for the forced-labour ban. A product passport's data follows its delegated act; with none adopted, design for it, never claim it. | S1, S9, S3, S2 |
| Specify | Each item carries its HS code and country of origin, and the landed cost follows the destination's low-value rules. | S10 |
| Implement | EDI ingest is idempotent by interchange control number, acknowledges each interchange, and validates against the partner's X12 release or EDIFACT directory. | S5, S7 |
| Implement | Every quantity is stored with its unit of measure; conversions live in one place, with their factors tested. | S7 |
| Implement | Traceability events are recorded as GS1 EPCIS 2.0 events (what, when, where, why), so a recall is one query. | S4 |
| Review | Out-of-order and duplicate carrier events, a resent interchange, and each unit conversion have a test. | S7, S5 |
| Roll out | Stuck shipments, EDI rejects, and unacknowledged interchanges are rollback triggers and observe signals. | S7, S5 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shipment state machine tests | every carrier event moves a shipment along an allowed transition, once | property-based tests over event sequences, duplicates and out-of-order events included | S7 |
| EDI replay test | a resent interchange is processed once and acknowledged again | an integration test that feeds one fixture interchange twice with the same control number | S5, S7 |
| EDI conformance check | every outbound document validates against the partner's implementation guide | the EDI translator's validator, or a schema of the partner's guide, over fixture documents in CI | S5 |
| GS1 key check digit tests | every GTIN and SSCC created or accepted has a valid check digit and length | unit tests of the mod-10 check digit, with GS1's published examples as fixtures | S4 |
| Unit conversion tests | no quantity is stored without its unit, and each conversion round-trips | property-based tests over the conversion table, and a schema check that every quantity column has a unit column | S7 |
| Due diligence traceability test | every EUDR lot shipped carries a statement reference after splits and blends | an integration test over receiving, splitting, blending, and shipping | S1 |
| Denied-party screening test | a shipment to a listed party, or a controlled item without its classification, is held before it ships | an integration test in CI with fixture parties from each screened list and a controlled item | S8 |

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/industry-standards.json`.
